findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox items instead of plain `**Commit**:` lines
findings.description: All 17 commit markers in this file are written as checklist items (`- [ ] Commit: \`feat: ...\``, e.g. lines 112, 157, 187, 217, 264, 320, 508, 527), rather than plain `**Commit**: \`...\`` lines. This deviates from the repo's established convention — every other task file I checked (e.g. `144-tasks.utility-actions.md`, `128-tasks.review-transport-unification-provider-decoupling.md`) uses the plain non-checkbox `**Commit**:` form, which is what the review convention calls for ("plain lines, never checkboxes"). Any tooling that greps for `**Commit**:` to find tested commit points will find none here. The placement itself is correct (after impl+test pairs, not every task, not only at the end), so only the marker format needs fixing.

findings.title: All functional, technical and integration success criteria trace to tasks with correct test-with sequencing
findings.description: Every success criterion maps to a task: owner/heartbeat/progress (Tasks 8, 11–14), orphaned listing + wait exit 8 (19, 20, 22), stale policy (19, 20, 22, 33–35), v4 UNOWNED behaviour (8, 20, 22), foreground stall + dispatch mapping (15–18), prune selection/protection/deletion (32–39), no per-run warnings + summary line (21, 22, 25, 26), column fitter and no-box pipelines list (23–28), pipelines show (29–31). Each implementation task is immediately followed by its test task(s) with a commit at the tested point; the spike (Task 2) precedes D7 work, `ActiveItem` is defined once in Task 4 and explicitly not redefined in Task 8, `run_liveness` (9–10) precedes its consumers (19, 21, 33), and the report pattern (32) precedes `apply_prune` (36). No scope-creep task found; Task 41 (issue) and Task 42 (verification) trace to Implementation Notes step 8 and the Verification Walkthrough.

findings.title: Restated listing-time NFR has a load test that CI already gates
findings.description: The slice restates the "under 1 s with a few hundred run-state files" NFR in Success Criteria; Task 22a adds `tests/load/test_run_listing_scale.py` with a `MAX_LISTING_S = 1.0` wall-clock assertion and row-count check, modelled on the existing `tests/load/test_usage_reader_loop.py`. I confirmed the task's claim that no new CI wiring is needed: `pyproject.toml` sets `testpaths = ["tests"]` with no exclude, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `uv run pytest` (plus the hermetic job), so `tests/load/` is collected and gated on every CI run — the four existing load tests are gated the same way. Gating is explicitly documented in the task rather than left implicit.

findings.title: Load test adds a time assertion the design deliberately omitted — consistent with review requirements
findings.description: The design's Special Considerations state "There is still no assertion on time in tests" and rely on walkthrough step 8 for wall-clock measurement. Task 22a introduces a hard 1.0 s assertion, a small addition beyond the design text, but it is appropriate: the review criteria require a load test when the slice restates an NFR, and the bound is described as generous for CI jitter. No action needed; noted only for awareness of the design/task difference.
